nodes.name: 02:30 IST daily
nodes.notes: GENERIC_TIMEZONE is Asia/Kolkata (set in the Dockerfile), so this cron is IST, not UTC.

parameters.query:
-- Independent verification that the recompute upstream actually landed.
-- Deliberately NOT trusting the HTTP 200 from 'Trigger recompute': this
-- re-reads the result through the READ-ONLY cadence_agent role, so a write
-- that reported success but wrote nothing still fails the workflow.
--
-- Checks COVERAGE (how many customers have a score), not FRESHNESS -- there
-- is deliberately no `where computed_at > ...` filter. An earlier version
-- had one and false-failed on every machine where nobody had run the job in
-- the last 24h. computed_at is still selected so a human can see it.
select count(*) as scored,
       max(computed_at) as computed_at
from v_customer_scores;

nodes.name: Score coverage check
nodes.notes: Read-only cadence_agent role, on purpose: this node verifies the write the previous node asked for, and a verifier that shares the writer’s privileges verifies less. The recompute is triggered by the HTTP node upstream, which calls POST /api/internal/recompute-scores.

nodes.name: Fewer scored than expected?
nodes.notes: ~800 customers have a score in a healthy state. Under 700 after a recompute means the run upstream partly failed, or the customer table grew faster than scoring covers it — worth knowing before the morning outreach in workflow 03 reads incomplete scores.

parameters.jsCode: return [{ json: { ok: true, scored: $json.scored, computed_at: $json.computed_at } }];

nodes.name: Trigger recompute
nodes.notes: Calls POST /api/internal/recompute-scores, which runs db/scoring.sql for every customer (~1s for 801). host.docker.internal is how this container reaches the app on the host -- plain localhost here would mean the container itself. PORT: set to 3000; change it if your dev server comes up on 3001. The secret is an n8n credential (x-cadence-trigger-secret), not a container env var. This node is the ONLY thing in n8n that can write scores -- the coverage check downstream deliberately keeps the read-only cadence_agent role.
